title: Actions and naturality of the balanced derived tensor model
statement: For the balanced model $P\otimes_R F$ of $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], multiplication by $a\in A$ on $P$ induces the action of the corresponding endomorphism of $M$ in $D(A)$; each $b\in R'$ acts on $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ through the endomorphism of $R'$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$, and these commuting actions make every $H^i(P\otimes_R F)$ an $A\otimes_R R'$-module. The canonical isomorphisms between the models for different choices of $P$ and $F$, and their identification with $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$, are $A\otimes_R R'$-linear on cohomology and natural in $M$; and under them the canonical comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R R')$ is represented by the chain map $P\otimes_R F\to P\otimes_R R'=P\otimes_A(A\otimes_R R')$ induced by $F\to R'$, whose effect on each $H^i$ is $A\otimes_R R'$-linear.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), functoriality and module actions of the derived tensor; equation comparison-map

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions $P\to M$ over $A$ and $F\to R'$ over $R$. By [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], $C=P\otimes_R F$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ in $D(A)$, multiplication by elements of $R'$ gives commuting endomorphisms in $D(A)$ and hence an $A\otimes_R R'$-module structure on each $H^i(C)$, and the construction is independent of the resolutions up to canonical isomorphism and functorial in $M$. The $A$-action is that of $C$ as a complex of $A$-modules: multiplication by $a$ on $P$ tensored with $1_F$, which is compatible under $P\to M$ with multiplication by $a$ on $M$, so it induces the corresponding endomorphism of $M$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, K-flat model and functoriality paragraph

proof.text: Write $C=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R P)$ and apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to the exact functors $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N:D(R)\to D(A)$ for the $A$-complexes $N=P$ and $N=M$. The action of $b\in R'$ is the value of this functor on the morphism of $R'$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$; by clause (2) the canonical isomorphisms between the models for two K-flat resolutions $F,F'$ of $R'$ are those of a functor, so they commute with these values, and they are $A$-linear because they are morphisms in $D(A)$. By clause (3), a chain map $u:N\to N'$ of $A$-complexes gives a natural transformation represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$, which is a quasi-isomorphism when $u$ is; taking $u$ the resolution $P\to M$, or a map $P\to P'$ over $M$ between two K-flat resolutions, shows that the identifications of $C$ with $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ and between choices of $P$ commute with the action of $b$ (naturality in the first variable) and of $a$ (compatibility with composition, $u$ being $A$-linear). Hence all these isomorphisms are $A\otimes_R R'$-linear on cohomology, and clause (3) for a chain map $M\to M'$ gives naturality in $M$.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), independence of choices and functoriality

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-transitivity] with $B=R'$, $T=C=A\otimes_R R'$, $K=M$, $P_K=P$, $Q=F$, $K'=P\otimes_A T$ (a complex of $T$-modules representing $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T$, since $P$ is K-flat over $A$) and $\psi$ the identity. The comparison morphism $c_M:M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T$ is then represented by $P\otimes_R F\to P\otimes_R R'=P\otimes_A T$, the chain map induced by $F\to R'$ followed by the associativity identification (the last map to $P\otimes_A C$ being the identity), and $\varphi_M=c_M$ commutes with the action of every $b\in R'$, so each $H^i(c_M)$ is $A\otimes_R R'$-linear. By Step 2 this holds for every choice of $P$ and $F$ under the canonical identifications.
